claim: Antibodies are a major component of adaptive immunity against invading pathogens.
source: Antibodies are a major component of adaptive immunity against invading pathogens.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in immunology, representing established scientific consensus.

claim: The available repertoire of antibodies is unique in individuals and constantly shifting in response to immunological pressure.
source: The available repertoire of antibodies is unique in individuals and constantly shifting in response to immunological pressure under which activation, selection, proliferation, maturation, and differentiation of the antibody-producing B-cells takes place (Lam et al., 2020; Tellier and Nutt, 2019; Pieper et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Current methods to determine the antigen-specific antibody repertoire rely on single (memory) B-cell sorting, followed by targeted sequencing of the coding mRNAs for the heavy and light chains.
source: Current methods to determine the antigen-specific antibody repertoire rely on single (memory) B-cell sorting, followed by targeted sequencing of the coding mRNAs for the heavy and light chains (Georgiou et al., 2014; Lavinder et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research describing these methods.

claim: Antibodies function as circulating glycoproteins in bodily fluid, secreted from plasma cells which are in turn derived from diverse pools of memory B cells located in various tissues.
source: Antibodies function as circulating glycoproteins in bodily fluid, secreted from plasma cells which are in turn derived from diverse pools of memory B cells located in various tissues, including bone marrow, spleen, lymph nodes, and only to a minor degree in blood (Inoue and Kurosaki, 2024; Meng et al., 2017; Akkaya et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on antibody biology and B cell distribution.

claim: Using a bottom-up proteomics approach, antibody-derived peptides can be sequenced de novo from fragmentation spectra and assembled into full heavy/light chain sequences.
source: First, using a bottom-up proteomics approach, antibody-derived peptides can be sequenced de novo from fragmentation spectra and assembled into full heavy/light chain sequences (Lavinder et al., 2015; de Graaf et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research demonstrating this approach.

claim: Sequence accuracy from bottom-up proteomics is such that functional monoclonal antibodies can be reconstructed from the input data.
source: Sequence accuracy is such that functional monoclonal antibodies can be reconstructed from the input data, and several reports have described successful sequencing efforts of human serum, milk, and urine-derived antibodies (Fridy et al., 2014; Peng et al., 2023b; Bondt et al., 2024; Peng et al., 2023a; Tran et al., 2016; Bondt et al., 2021; Sousa et al., 2012; Sen et al., 2017; Rickert et al., 2016; Savidor et al., 2017; Peng et al., 2021; Guthals et al., 2017; Cheung et al., 2012; Castellana et al., 2011; Bandeira et al., 2008; Dupré et al., 2021; Peng et al., 2025).
evidence: Supported by extensive citations to prior research demonstrating successful antibody reconstruction.

claim: Ward and colleagues reported that with EMPEM they obtained near-atomic resolution reconstructions by cryoEM to resolve side-chain densities in the epitope-paratope region.
source: Ward and colleagues have reported that with the latter approach, which they coined Electron Microscopy based Polyclonal Epitope Mapping (EMPEM), they obtained near-atomic resolution reconstructions by cryoEM to resolve side-chain densities in the epitope-paratope region (Antanasijevic et al., 2022a).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research by Ward and colleagues.

claim: The benchmark dataset includes 164 maps, including Fabs from human, rabbit, mouse, and macaque species.
source: The final benchmark includes 164 maps, including Fabs from human, rabbit, mouse, and macaque species.
evidence: Direct statement about the composition of the benchmark dataset assembled for this study.

claim: Of the 164 input maps, 141 and 144 yielded a non-zero alignment score for the heavy and light chains in the Stitch result, respectively.
source: Of the 164 input maps, 141 and 144 yielded a non-zero alignment score for the heavy and light chains in the Stitch result, respectively.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results from the benchmark analysis.

claim: 152 maps were analyzed further to evaluate the sequence accuracy of this approach.
source: These add up to a total of 152 maps which were analyzed further to evaluate the sequence accuracy of this approach (including 134 maps with a non-zero alignment score for both heavy and light chain).
evidence: Direct statement about the number of maps included in the analysis.

claim: The 15% rate of sequencing errors exceeds the typical levels of somatic hypermutation observed in mature antibody sequences, which are on the order of 1–10%.
source: The 15% rate of sequencing errors exceeds the typical levels of somatic hypermutation observed in mature antibody sequences, which are on the order of 1–10%.
evidence: Combines experimental data (15% error rate) with established knowledge about somatic hypermutation rates.

claim: The top scoring V-genes from the ModelAngelo sequences have significantly higher pairwise identities than a random draw from the V-gene repertoire in IMGT for both the heavy and light chains (p<0.0001).
source: As shown in Figure 3, the top scoring V-genes from the ModelAngelo sequences have significantly higher pairwise identities than a random draw from the V-gene repertoire in IMGT for both the heavy and light chains (p<0.0001 in unpaired, two-tailed Kolmogorov Smirnov tests).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The mean/median V-gene identity in a random draw from the IMGT repertoire is 0.59/0.52 and 0.56/0.53 for the heavy and light chains, respectively.
source: The mean/median V-gene identity in a random draw from the IMGT repertoire is 0.59/0.52 and 0.56/0.53 for the heavy and light chains, respectively.
evidence: Direct statement of statistical analysis results from the benchmark.

claim: With the ModelAngelo-derived sequences, V-gene identity improves to 0.78/0.87 and 0.75/0.85 for the heavy and light chains in the full dataset.
source: With the ModelAngelo-derived sequences this improves to 0.78/0.87 and 0.75/0.85 for the heavy and light chains in the full dataset.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results comparing ModelAngelo performance to random baseline.

claim: V-gene identity gradually improves with higher alignment scores to 0.89/1.00 and 0.88/1.00 for heavy and light chains, starting at a cutoff of 80.
source: This gradually improves with higher alignment scores to 0.89/1.00 and 0.88/1.00 for heavy and light chains, starting at a cutoff of 80 (representing 92/141 and 80/134 maps for heavy and light chain, respectively).
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results showing correlation between alignment score and accuracy.

claim: The complete complementarity determining regions CDRH3 and CDRL3 were covered in 66 and 68 maps for the heavy and light chain, respectively.
source: The complete complementarity determining regions CDRH3 and CDRL3 were covered in 66 and 68 maps for the heavy and light chain, respectively, see Figure 4.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results with reference to Figure 4.

claim: The length of the complete antigen binding loops was estimated with an average error of 0.5±3.3 or 1.7±6.0 residues for heavy and light chain.
source: The length of the complete antigen binding loops was estimated with an average error of 0.5±3.3 or 1.7±6.0 residues for heavy and light chain, with average sequence identities of 0.63 and 0.41.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results quantifying CDR3 length estimation accuracy.

claim: The global FSC resolution of the input map is a poor predictor of both the Stitch alignment score and the inferred V-gene identity.
source: We found the global FSC resolution of the input map to be a poor predictor of both the Stitch alignment score and the inferred V-gene identity, likely because it is dominated by the bulk of the antigen and not representative of the local resolution in the epitope-paratope region as shown in Figure 5.
evidence: Experimental observation with mechanistic inference about why global resolution is not predictive.

claim: CR3022 antibody was isolated from a convalescent survivor of a SARS-CoV infection and targets a cryptic, but conserved epitope at the base of the Spike receptor-binding domain, with cross-neutralization to SARS-CoV-2.
source: This antibody was isolated from a convalescent survivor of a SARS-CoV infection and targets a cryptic, but conserved epitope at the base of the Spike receptor-binding domain, with cross-neutralization to SARS-CoV-2 (ter Meulen et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research characterizing the CR3022 antibody.

claim: The CR3022 antibody consists of an IGHV5-51 heavy chain, paired with an IGKV4-1 light chain.
source: The antibody consists of an IGHV5-51 heavy chain, paired with an IGKV4-1 light chain.
evidence: Direct statement about the known V-gene composition of CR3022.

claim: When using the CR3022 map as input for ModelAngelo and subsequently Stitch, the IGHV5-51 and IGKV4-1 germline sequences are correctly identified based on their alignment scores.
source: When using this map as input for ModelAngelo and subsequently Stitch, the IGHV5-51 and IGKV4-1 germline sequences are correctly identified based on their alignment scores.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results for the CR3022 test case.

claim: When using the reconstructed variable domains as templates to guide assembly of the de novo peptide reads from LC-MS/MS data, the final consensus sequences are 96% and 99% identical to the true heavy and light chain respectively.
source: When using these reconstructed variable domains as templates to guide assembly of the de novo peptide reads from the LC-MS/MS data published by Person and colleagues (Gadush et al., 2022), the final consensus sequences are 96% and 99% identical to the true heavy and light chain respectively.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results demonstrating improved accuracy with ModelAngelo-derived templates.

claim: The only three remaining errors in the six CDR sequences are I/L assignments, which have identical masses and are notoriously challenging for MS-based sequencing.
source: Of note, the only three remaining errors in the six CDR sequences are I/L assignments, which have identical masses and are notoriously challenging for MS-based sequencing.
evidence: Combines experimental observation with established knowledge about I/L ambiguity in mass spectrometry.

claim: For the CR3022 dataset from the monoclonal antibody, the LC-MS/MS data alone assembled with Stitch against the full range of V-genes yields an accuracy of 97% and 98% for the heavy and light chain, respectively.
source: For this CR3022 dataset, derived from the monoclonal antibody, the LC-MS/MS data alone assembled with Stitch against the full range of V-genes already yields a similar accuracy of 97% and 98% for the heavy and light chain, respectively.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results for LC-MS/MS-only analysis.

claim: The sequence accuracy plummets to below 0.6 when the background consists of five additional monoclonal antibodies in a 5:1 ratio to the target input reads.
source: By contrast, the sequence accuracy plummets to below 0.6 when the background consists of the five additional monoclonal antibodies in a 5:1 ratio to the target input reads.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results showing impact of monoclonal background on accuracy.

claim: The accuracy is recovered to >0.95 when using either the true CR3022 sequences or the ModelAngelo-derived templates.
source: The accuracy is recovered to >0.95 when using either the true CR3022 sequences or the ModelAngelo-derived templates.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results demonstrating template-guided assembly improves accuracy.

claim: 46 published EMPEM maps were downloaded from EMDB.
source: We downloaded all 46 published EMPEM maps from EMDB, of which 23 were of sufficient quality to give a non-zero alignment score when using the ModelAngelo results in Stitch (see Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Direct statement about the number of EMPEM maps analyzed.

claim: 23 of the 46 EMPEM maps were of sufficient quality to give a non-zero alignment score when using the ModelAngelo results in Stitch.
source: We downloaded all 46 published EMPEM maps from EMDB, of which 23 were of sufficient quality to give a non-zero alignment score when using the ModelAngelo results in Stitch (see Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results from EMPEM map analysis.

claim: Of the 23 EMPEM maps with non-zero scores, 8 have alignment scores above 50 for both heavy and light chain.
source: Of the 23 maps, 8 have alignment scores above 50 for both heavy and light chain, at which point we estimate the mean/median V-gene identity to be approximately 0.85/0.90.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results from EMPEM map analysis.

claim: At alignment scores above 50, the mean/median V-gene identity is estimated to be approximately 0.85/0.90.
source: Of the 23 maps, 8 have alignment scores above 50 for both heavy and light chain, at which point we estimate the mean/median V-gene identity to be approximately 0.85/0.90.
evidence: Inference based on the benchmark analysis applied to the EMPEM dataset.

claim: ModelAngelo-derived templates are useful for sequence assembly against complex polyclonal backgrounds.
source: These results demonstrate that ModelAngelo-derived templates are useful for sequence assembly against complex polyclonal backgrounds.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the experimental results with CR3022 and background mixtures.

claim: Experimental EMPEM studies may yield sufficiently detailed reconstructions of the antigen-antibody complexes to narrow down the candidate V-genes of the resolved Fabs accurately.
source: This analysis shows that experimental EMPEM studies may yield sufficiently detailed reconstructions of the antigen-antibody complexes to narrow down the candidate V-genes of the resolved Fabs accurately.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the analysis of published EMPEM maps.

claim: Heavy-light chain pairing is a problematic blind spot to proteomics sequencing, as the antibodies are denatured and digested as part of the sample workup.
source: Second, heavy-light chain pairing is a problematic blind spot to proteomics sequencing, as the antibodies are denatured and digested as part of the sample workup.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge about proteomics sample preparation methods.

claim: Heavy-light chain pairing is trivial in cryoEM data as the chains are in direct contact in the resolved Fabs in the map.
source: In contrast, this pairing is trivial in cryoEM data as the chains are in direct contact in the resolved Fabs in the map.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge about cryoEM structure determination.

claim: Reconstruction of CDRH3 is especially challenging with proteomics data alone, as it spans the junction between the recombined V-, D-, and J-segments.
source: Finally, reconstruction of CDRH3 is especially challenging with proteomics data alone, as it spans the junction between the recombined V-, D-, and J-segments, of which the D-segment is short and hypervariable to a point that germline sequences do not provide a functional template for sequence assembly.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge about antibody gene recombination and proteomics limitations.

claim: Both EMPEM and MS-based polyclonal antibody sequencing are still limited to the top 1–10 antibodies in the polyclonal mixture.
source: We believe that both EMPEM and MS-based polyclonal antibody sequencing are still limited to the top 1–10 antibodies in the polyclonal mixture.
evidence: Speculative statement about current limitations of the methods.

claim: The EMPEM approach is biased towards bigger and well-ordered target antigens.
source: The EMPEM approach is biased towards bigger and well-ordered target antigens, which calls for additional complementary approaches like HDX-MS for a comprehensive polyclonal epitope mapping exercise.
evidence: Inference about methodological limitations based on the nature of cryoEM structure determination.

claim: The benchmark dataset was searched for published maps containing antigen-binding fragments (Fabs) of any species, at nominal resolutions of ≤4 Ångström, released after April 1st 2022.
source: We searched the EMDB for published maps containing antigen-binding fragments (Fabs) of any species, at nominal resolutions of ≤4 Ångström, released after the training data for ModelAngelo was obtained (April 1st 2022).
evidence: Direct description of the methodology used to assemble the benchmark dataset.

claim: The search for benchmark maps was performed on February 11th 2023 at the EMDB website.
source: The search was performed on February 11th 2023 at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/emdb/ using the search term 'antibody fab resolution:[* TO 4] AND release_date:[2022-03-31T00:00:00Z TO 2023-11-02T00:00:00Z] sample_name:*fab* fitted_pdbs:[* TO *]'.
evidence: Direct description of the methodology including specific search parameters.

claim: Stitch was extended to allow mmCIF files as input.
source: Stitch was extended to allow mmCIF files as input.
evidence: Direct statement about software modifications made for this study.

claim: ModelAngelo outputs a confidence score per residue in the B-factor column of the mmCIF input.
source: ModelAngelo outputs a confidence score per residue in the B-factor column of the mmCIF input, which was used as a local confidence for the sequence.
evidence: Direct statement about how ModelAngelo output was processed.

claim: The local confidence from ModelAngelo is used as weight in determining the consensus sequence of overlapping polypeptides, following assembly in Stitch.
source: Second, the local confidence is used as weight in determining the consensus sequence of overlapping polypeptides, following assembly in Stitch.
evidence: Direct description of the methodology for consensus sequence determination.

claim: The deposited model mmCIF and EM maps for the full benchmark were downloaded and ran with ModelAngelo (version 1.01) in 'build_no_seq' mode.
source: The deposited model mmCIF and EM maps for the full benchmark were downloaded and ran with ModelAngelo (version 1.01) in 'build_no_seq' mode.
evidence: Direct description of the computational analysis methodology.

claim: The identity of the inferred V-gene with the true sequence scales with the alignment scores in Stitch.
source: Furthermore, the identity of the inferred V-gene with the true sequence scales with the alignment scores in Stitch, making it a valuable metric for the quality of the V-gene inference.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The moderately better length and sequence accuracy of CDRH3 compared to CDRL3 in ModelAngelo output reflects the CDRH3's notoriously tight involvement in antigen binding.
source: While CDRH3 is the more challenging region in MS-based approaches to antibody sequencing, we believe that the moderately better length and sequence accuracy of CDRH3 compared to CDRL3 in ModelAngelo output reflects the CDRH3's notoriously tight involvement in antigen binding, hence a greater relative stability in the antibody-antigen complex, resulting in better order in the reconstructed EM density maps.
evidence: Mechanistic inference to explain observed differences in CDRH3 vs CDRL3 accuracy.

claim: The global FSC resolution is likely dominated by the bulk of the antigen and not representative of the local resolution in the epitope-paratope region.
source: We found the global FSC resolution of the input map to be a poor predictor of both the Stitch alignment score and the inferred V-gene identity, likely because it is dominated by the bulk of the antigen and not representative of the local resolution in the epitope-paratope region as shown in Figure 5.
evidence: Inference to explain why global resolution is not predictive of sequencing accuracy.

claim: The sequence assembly with Stitch is already tolerant to the diffuse polyclonal background from the whole IgG fraction.
source: The analysis confirmed that even without ModelAngelo-derived templates, the sequence assembly with Stitch is already tolerant to the diffuse polyclonal background from the whole IgG fraction, yielding a similar accuracy as in the absence of these background peptides.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results from the background mixing analysis.

claim: There is a gain in accuracy by using decoy templates with the LC-MS/MS data alone, although smaller compared to the use of ModelAngelo-derived templates.
source: There is also a gain in accuracy by using decoy templates with the LC-MS/MS data alone, although smaller compared to the use of ModelAngelo-derived templates.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental results comparing different template strategies.

claim: Map quality is a critical bottleneck for deriving antibody sequences from cryoEM reconstructions.
source: We demonstrate that while map quality is a critical bottleneck, it is possible to sequence antibody variable domains from cryoEM reconstructions with accuracies of up to 80–90%.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the benchmark analysis results.

claim: It is possible to sequence antibody variable domains from cryoEM reconstructions with accuracies of up to 80–90%.
source: We demonstrate that while map quality is a critical bottleneck, it is possible to sequence antibody variable domains from cryoEM reconstructions with accuracies of up to 80–90%.
evidence: Direct statement of the main finding from the benchmark analysis.

claim: The rate of errors from ModelAngelo sequencing exceeds the typical levels of somatic hypermutation.
source: While the rate of errors exceeds the typical levels of somatic hypermutation, we show that the ModelAngelo-derived sequences can be used to assign the used V-genes.
evidence: Comparison of observed error rates with known biological variation rates.

claim: ModelAngelo-derived sequences can be used to assign the used V-genes.
source: While the rate of errors exceeds the typical levels of somatic hypermutation, we show that the ModelAngelo-derived sequences can be used to assign the used V-genes.
evidence: Direct statement of a key finding from the study.

claim: ModelAngelo-derived sequences provide a functional guide to assemble de novo peptides from LC-MS/MS data more accurately.
source: This provides a functional guide to assemble de novo peptides from LC-MS/MS data more accurately and improves the tolerance to a background of polyclonal antibody sequences.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the CR3022 proof-of-principle experiment.

claim: ModelAngelo-derived sequences improve the tolerance to a background of polyclonal antibody sequences.
source: This provides a functional guide to assemble de novo peptides from LC-MS/MS data more accurately and improves the tolerance to a background of polyclonal antibody sequences.
evidence: Direct statement of a key finding from the background mixing experiments.
